name: Quell Open-Structure Trail Sandal
description: A heavy-duty trail sandal built for outdoor use — thick lugged rubber sole, webbing straps over a contoured footbed, and a completely open frame that imposes no shape on whatever foot is wearing it. The webbing system has six adjustment points including a heel cage. It handles digitigrade feet, hooves, clawed toes, wide splays — anything that can bear weight on a footbed. Looks utilitarian and outdoorsy. Worn by Tier 2-3 geneware users who do physical work outdoors or spend time in the peri-urban fringe zones.
functionality: Six-point adjustable webbing system with heel cage accommodates any foot morphology. Lugged sole rated for rough terrain.
what_it_says: You work outside, you have modified feet, and you've got better things to worry about than looking polished.
worn_by: geneware users who hike or work rough terrain
story_hooks: A Quell sandal was recovered from a collapsed structure in the fringe — the wearer's body wasn't found, but the sandal's footbed holds a clear impression of a hoof.
Quell's webbing supplier switched materials last season — the new batch frays faster and people are talking.

physical_description.visual_profile: A skeletal, modular sandal with an aggressive stance. Open framework reveals the foot entirely—no enclosing walls or toe boxes. Thick lugged sole dominates visually, creating a rugged, utilitarian silhouette. Webbing straps crisscross in a technical lattice pattern. Looks purpose-built and uncompromising.
physical_description.fit: Completely adaptive—zero structural constraints. Contoured footbed accommodates digitigrade, ungulate, and clawed morphologies equally. Six adjustment points allow infinite micro-fitting. Heel cage stabilizes without clamping.
physical_description.primary_material: High-grip vulcanized rubber sole with aggressive lug pattern. Reinforced synthetic webbing straps in mil-spec ballistic weave. Contoured footbed is molded polyurethane with drainage channels.
physical_description.texture: Sole is deeply textured with geometric lugs for mud/rock grip. Webbing has a stiff, technical feel—slightly fuzzy against skin, designed to resist fraying. Footbed surface is slightly tacky and dimpled for traction.
physical_description.color_scheme: Military grey-green rubber sole. Webbing in charcoal or burnt orange. Footbed in neutral tan with darker grip zones. Minimal branding—small Φ-stamped metal adjustment points.
physical_description.closures: Six friction-fit webbing adjustment points along the midfoot and heel. Pull-tight mechanism with heat-sealed stops. No buckles or magnetic snaps—purely mechanical, field-repairable.
distinctive_features: Completely open frame—no toe box or heel cup
Six independent webbing adjustment zones for custom fit
Heel cage strap with triple-pass webbing
Oversized lug pattern rated for loose substrate
Field-replaceable sole option available through Quell service centers
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2-3 functional/outdoor. Expensive enough to signal investment in quality gear (Φ180-220 range), but purely performance-oriented with no luxury markers.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by outdoor workers, geneware users with non-human foot morphology, peri-urban fringe dwellers, and corporate environmental teams. Signals competence in rough terrain, acceptance of non-standard biology, and self-reliance.
physical_description.condition_typical: Usually scuffed and mud-caked. Webbing shows wear but holds. Sole develops personalized wear patterns from user's gait. Well-maintained pairs last 18+ months. Patched straps are common field modifications.
